strategy.title: No plan until the inspection-certificate pack's price is established
strategy.why: The only opening's price is contradicted: the card records 120000 cents ($1,200) while its sourced price fact says $120. At $1,200, 5 deals carry $6,000 and 140 licensed contractors at the measured 12% close yield about 16, so the plan would work; at $120, 50 deals are needed and the whole reachable market at 12% yields about 17 deals, about $2,016. Which is true decides the plan, and nothing on the card says which, so no executable or conditional plan is established.

alternatives.title: Sell at $1,200 anyway and measure
alternatives.why: No source shows any contractor paying $1,200; the only sourced price is $120, so a $1,200 offer is an unestablished price, not a test of an unknown close rate.

noPlan.decisiveGap: The price is contradicted ($1,200 on the card vs a sourced $120): at $1,200 the target needs 5 of ~17 expected closes and is reachable; at $120 the whole 140-contractor market yields about $2,016, short of $6,000. No figure establishes which.
noPlan.resolution: Research the published or invoiced price contractors pay for this pack and the price at which the 12/100 close was measured; if $1,200 is confirmed, sell 5-6 packs by email to the state board's licensee list (cash in 8 days); if $120, record that this opening cannot carry the target and look for a second opening.

review.reasons: NO_PLAN is right, and the decisive gap is named correctly as the price, which the card's own evidence contradicts (priceCents 120000 = $1,200 vs the sourced price fact $120); Brain's links[] also mark OFFER_AND_PRICE unestablished ('no single price on the card'). Recomputed: at $120, 140 licensees buying ~once a year x 12% measured close ~ 16.8 deals ~ $2,016 < $6,000 (Brain's MARKET_VOLUME is also unestablished at that price); at $1,200, 5 deals = $6,000 out of ~17 expected. No constraint is asserted from missing evidence. The resolution (establish the paid price and the price at which 12/100 closed) is the right next step, and refusing to sell at an unsourced $1,200 is correct.
